symptom: An import mapping cannot declare its INPUT OBJECT, so a custom handler's `Param: parameter` refers to something that cannot exist, and `describe` of a real one drops the declaration while still emitting the handler that uses it
cause: Mendix stores it as `ParameterType`, a `DataTypes$ObjectType` naming the entity. Measured across the demo apps: 10 of 327 mappings declare one (GenAICommons.ChunkCollection in eight), 190 import mappings store the `DataTypes$UnknownType` marker, and an EXPORT mapping carries no `ParameterType` property at all (0 of 127) — its parameter IS its root object, so there is no export spelling. All three writers hardcoded the UnknownType variant
insight: `parameter Module.Entity` on the header, after the schema source. gen models **no** `ParameterType` property at all, so the modelsdk read goes to raw BSON — the route `customHandlerFromRaw` takes. **The legacy parser unmarshals a unit into `map[string]any`, so a nested sub-document arrives as `map[string]any`, NOT `bson.D`**: asserting `bson.D` compiles, always fails, and leaves DESCRIBE silently dropping the clause on the legacy engine only — caught solely by running the same assertions on both backends, so write that test. Two refusals, each with the guard stubbed and measured on mxbuild 11.13: `Param: parameter` with nothing declared is **CE0279** "Parameter is used in object handling microflow while the mapping does not specify one", and an unknown entity is refused by name. **Deliberately NOT guarded**: a parameter whose entity does not match the microflow's parameter type — mxbuild reports **CE0282** naming both types, and duplicating it in mxcli would need a generalisation-aware walk that could refuse valid specialisations. Check the whole thing over the BUILT model in `finishImportMapping`, not the AST, so the JSON-structure and message-definition builders are covered at once. Repro `mdl-examples/bug-tests/mapping-265-mapping-input-parameter.mdl`, tests `mdl/executor/mapping_parameter_test.go`. Issue ako/mxcli#265
